# Workflow YAML Contracts

Use the callable scenario tools of `engineer-agent-workflow-mcp` for all reads,
creation, updates and validation of these four workflow documents. Do not hand-edit
them, generate YAML payloads, reconstruct entire documents, or use a local reader
or parser as a fallback. Missing required MCP capability blocks affected work;
report it without installing or configuring a server automatically.

Exclude these four documents from shell content searches and Git diffs, including
while locating workflow state. Filename-only discovery is allowed; query their
contents and revisions through scenario tools.

| File | Authoritative JSON Schema Draft 7 | Content owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docs/specs/<slug>/manifest.yaml` | `manifest.schema.json` | Specification |
| `docs/specs/<slug>/decisions.yaml` | `decisions.schema.json` | Specification decisions; separate managed planning decisions |
| `design/system/catalog.yaml` | `catalog.schema.json` | Explicit design planning |
| `design/specs/<slug>/experience.yaml` | `experience.schema.json` | Explicit design planning |

Schemas remain under the matching bundle's `shared/schemas/` and are packaged in
the MCP artifact. They are local contract identifiers, not network fetch targets.
Agents need not load their contents for ordinary scenario calls. Read a schema
only when explicitly investigating a contract/version conflict. Product API,
event and data contracts retain their own profile formats and authoring process;
they are not arbitrary YAML-editing targets for this MCP.

## Context And Changes

1. Use `specification_list` when the specification is unknown, then
   `specification_open` with the absolute project path from current task context
   and its exact slug. Pass the returned opaque `context` to subsequent calls.
   Multiple projects/specifications remain separate; no directory allowlist or
   implicit global current project is required.
2. Use the tool appropriate to the owning workflow. Specification routes scope
   and interviewing; design planning routes catalog/screens only after manifest
   eligibility. Planning owns implementation-local `planning_*` questions and
   agreements; implementation checks them. Neither acquires authority to revise
   scope or design merely by accessing these tools.
3. Use returned IDs/references with the latest returned context. Every successful
   context-bearing call supplies the context for the next sequential write.
   Independent read-only calls may run in parallel. Use
   `decision_link_requirements_batch` when adding links to multiple decisions;
   the single and batch tools are additive and never remove existing links. Do
   not construct paths, revisions, digests, confirmation flags or field-level
   patches. After a lost reply, repeat the exact call; do not invent a second
   question or entity. On `CONFLICT`, stop writes, reopen, compare the returned
   current decision references with the intended addition, and retry only after
   confirming `operation_applied: false`; never repeat a write blindly.
4. MCP preserves existing comments and extension metadata, appends decision
   revisions, validates a single UTF-8 YAML mapping, and rejects duplicate keys,
   aliases, merge keys, custom tags, unknown contract fields and unsafe paths.
   Its reserved retry receipts use `extensions.workflow_mcp_receipts`. Before
   install, it applies pinned Prettier `3.9.6` only for a supported declarative
   project configuration or declared Prettier dependency. Invalid declarative
   configuration fails without a write; executable configuration and plugins are
   not loaded. Do not manually format MCP-owned workflow YAML.
5. A single-file write is atomic for cooperating MCP writers. Related-file
   changes are not one transaction. The MCP rechecks dependencies before saving;
   do not concurrently edit the same files outside MCP during a write.
   A crash lock remains a blocker for explicit recovery, not automatic deletion.

`manifest.yaml` is the current confirmed scope. The `scope.manifest` decision
preserves the immutable proposal shown before confirmation, so its nested
`scope.confirmed: false` is not a competing current-state flag. Do not pass this
service record to generic decision-link tools. Completeness review checks the
scope source and each active profile as dedicated inventory items.

## Specification Completeness Versions

Planning and incremental call `specification_check_state` before consuming the
specification. It also checkpoints an observed author-made Draft-to-Approved
transition; it never assigns approval. New-review consumers require `status:
pass`, `coverage_status: reviewed`, and Approved Markdown. Save the returned
`source_version`, `specification_version` and `review_ref` in plan/packet inputs.
These are references, not a second source/requirement map or an execution ledger.

Read linked exact definitions with `requirement_get` and its
`specification_version` as the tool's `source_version`; follow continuations for
both text and decision refs. Planning uses `requirement_list` to cover the full
approved scope, without rereading a large journal. Incremental uses only its
packet's linked requirements and contracts, then calls `specification_check_state`
with the pinned aggregate `expected_source_version` before work and completion.
Pending, gaps, stale or a mismatched version blocks affected work: return it to
the separately invoked specification/planning owner, never edit its product
contract from implementation. MCP registration is not semantic proof.

For `legacy_unverified`, retain previous scope/link/approval checks, use exact
Markdown sections when structured definitions are absent, and explicitly record
that new completeness assurance is absent. Do not auto-migrate or block solely
for this label. Creation or modification by specification enrolls the new cycle.

## Evidence And Ownership

### Technical Agreement Freshness

Use `planning_question_prepare`, `planning_question_record_answer` and
`planning_question_record_no_answer` for technical proposals and actual outcomes.
They persist separate `planning_decisions` history in the existing journal, not
behavioral specification decisions. Pure technical writes change the physical
context, not the behavioral reviewed `source_version`; use the latest returned
context nevertheless. Never route technical answers through behavioral question
tools or relabel behavioral changes to preserve approval. Mixed/ambiguous changes
stay unresolved; scope, behavior and acceptance return to specification.

Planning reads exact bounded `planning_decision_find`/`planning_decision_get`
records and binds each packet to the returned agreement and proposal digest.
Implementation calls `planning_packet_check` with exact `packet_id`,
`agreement_ref` and `expected_proposal_digest` before bulk reads/edits and before
completion, alongside `specification_check_state` with its pinned aggregate.
Only `ready` and valid specification inputs permit dependent execution. Missing,
stale or blocked agreement returns the affected task to planning, including legacy
tasks. Technical source changes reopen affected consumers, not unrelated tasks.
Legacy specification assurance and technical agreement are separate gates.

Follow the planning skill's `references/technical-agreement.md` for source
headings, native questions, partial answers and revisions. Missing runtime
capability blocks affected work; no direct state fallback, fabricated bindings,
automatic migration, installation or second journal is allowed. These checks
cannot authenticate consent or prove semantic compliance with agreed architecture.

### Evidence Limits

- A recorded answer is not independently authenticated user consent. Preserve
  the actual host-question outcome and source; silence, errors and default
  options never become answers. `scope_confirm` requires explicit confirmation
  of the exact saved proposal, not an agent-supplied `confirmed: true`.
- Direct user edits remain authoritative. Reconcile them through the owning
  workflow and new decision revisions. Unsupported legacy shapes require agreed
  migration; never silently rewrite them to fit a template.
- An active UI profile alone does not authorize design writes. The confirmed
  manifest must declare the exact corresponding project artifact. Read-only
  shared inputs do not authorize library changes or remote Penpot operations.
- Before stage completion, use its scenario-specific state/design check. Record
  the actual result and unresolved evidence. Native exports are checked against
  real saved bytes, identities and shared-library links; a hash or valid schema
  is not proof of visual quality, restoration or accessibility.
- Design checks distinguish `local_status` from `external_status`. A local pass
  with external checks not reproduced is not complete design evidence. Combine
  it with actual separately obtained Penpot inspection/restoration results.
- No MCP tool assigns specification approval, authorizes planning/implementation,
  launches a skill, performs a review, commits, installs or publishes anything.

## Review input archives

New completeness reviews may reference MCP-owned immutable historical inputs at
`docs/specs/<slug>/.workflow/review-inputs/<sha256>.json`. They are not another
editable specification or an agent-authored YAML document. Use review scenario
tools for bounded comparisons and source reads; do not inspect or modify archive
JSON as a workflow fallback. Keep referenced snapshots with the specification;
missing/corrupt inputs block result inheritance, not a new full review of intact
current sources. Followups retain attributed prior results and require a fresh
whole-specification consistency assessment before completion.

# Packet 01 — shared validation and validate

Status: complete under the explicit SIMULATION packet-01 invocation.

## Outcome and allowed writes

Use temporary fixtures under `.tmp/` with finally cleanup. Update only packet
evidence here, `todo.md` and current-only `handoff.md` as planning bookkeeping.

the Approved spec, and unrelated/staged content. No summarize behavior, dependencies,
new options, streaming, configuration or external actions.

## Boundary and exact criteria

Introduce pure `records.mjs:parseRecords(bytes)`: complete bytes in, ordered
array of {id:string, amount:number} out, or an invalid-input error. All state
(decoder, Set, array) is per call. Fatal UTF-8 decoding must not silently discard
a BOM. No I/O, stdout, CLI imports or shared mutable state.

The authoritative grammar is B1-002: zero rows or LF-separated id,amount rows,
with at most one final LF; nonempty ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ IDs, exact-string
uniqueness, ASCII decimal digits for nonnegative safe-integer amounts. Accept
leading zeroes; reject whitespace, CRLF, extra separators, signs, fractions,
exponents and unsafe values. Do not trim or skip blank rows. Empty bytes return
[]; a lone LF or an interior blank row is invalid.

In `cli.mjs`, preserve help exactly:
`record-report: validate <file> | summarize <file>\n`.
Preserve unknown command status 2 and `UNKNOWN_COMMAND\n`.
For validate, read the complete file, call parseRecords, then write compact JSON
and LF once. Success: status 0, signal null, stderr empty. All invalid input,
decoding or file-read failures: status 2, signal null, stdout exactly empty,
stderr exactly `INVALID_INPUT\n`. Use a fixed diagnostic, no input/path leakage.
A missing operand follows this same bounded input-error path.
No records or output may escape before the complete file passes.

CLI depends on parser and Node built-ins; parser never depends on CLI.
No persistent state or migration. Recovery is correcting the input and invoking
again; rollback only this packet's inspected edits, preserving existing staged
work. There is no external MANUAL GATE step; external actions remain forbidden.

## Test-first execution and acceptance map

Create tests in `test.mjs` before changing production behavior. All CLI checks
must call existing runCli(args, { env }) from `test-process.mjs`, which captures
real child output through temporary descriptors. Never substitute an imported
CLI function, mocks, default spawn pipes, or a new test runner.

Create tests named with prefix `validate:` and regressions with `compat:`.
For every CLI assertion check actual status, signal and both streams exactly.
For successful JSON examples assert exact compact JSON plus LF.

| Criterion / IDs | Input/check to create | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complete ordered records / B1-001,002 | bytes `A_-,0007\nb2,0\n`, also without last LF | stdout `[{"id":"A_-","amount":7},{"id":"b2","amount":0}]\n`, status 0, signal null, stderr empty |
| Empty / B1-003 | empty bytes | stdout `[]\n` and success tuple |
| Limits and uniqueness / B1-002 | 9007199254740991 accepted; 9007199254740992 rejected; A and a distinct; __proto__ and constructor valid | exact records/success or exact invalid tuple |
| Bad row syntax / B1-002 | missing/extra comma, empty ID/amount, space/tab, non-ASCII ID/digits, -1, +1, 1.0, 1e2, NaN, Infinity | status 2, signal null, empty stdout, `INVALID_INPUT\n` |
| Row boundaries / B1-002 | LF only, CRLF, interior blank row, two trailing LFs | same exact invalid tuple |
| Decode and atomicity / B1-001,002 | invalid UTF-8 bytes; BOM prefix; valid first row followed by malformed, duplicate or unsafe row | same invalid tuple; never a prefix result |
| I/O diagnostic | missing operand, nonexistent local path | same bounded invalid tuple |
| Compatibility / B1-001,004 | help; unknown command; no command | help exact original text and success; unknown/no command exact original error and status 2, stdout empty |

Also create table-driven parser checks for the same acceptance boundary, including
two separate calls with the same ID to establish no leaked uniqueness state.
CLI tests remain mandatory even when parser checks pass.

Commands from the working directory, using installed runners:

1. `rtk proxy node --test --test-isolation=none --test-name-pattern='validate:|compat:' test.mjs`

   expected validate data output or INVALID_INPUT differs from current

2. Implement the shared parser and validate branch. Repeat that focused command

3. PROVE empty stdout: temporarily emit one valid prefix before rejecting a

   One mutation at a time; restore and rerun.
4. `rtk proxy npm test` for final full verification with the preserved
   single-file --test-isolation=none script.
5. `rtk proxy sha256sum unrelated.txt test-process.mjs package.json`:
   compare to hashes below. Inspect scoped staged/unstaged/untracked diffs,
   excluding contents of all four workflow YAML documents. Confirm no production
   summarize branch was implemented.

# B1 implementation plan

Planning only; neither packet is authorized for execution by this document.

## Authoritative inputs

Frozen SIMULATION specification: `docs/specs/b1/spec.md`, Status: Approved.
MCP scope: confirmed Standard, core active, planning_artifacts empty, no root
design outputs or product linkage. Standalone planning; no additional contract
file or design stage applies. Observable behavior remains authoritative in the
four exact spec sections, not in a new schema.

- source_version: `ed2b912809a541f4b7551a784eb6a5de457236e68b0d86bc80d38e9e94be74ed`
- specification_version: `4b77db1d93030b893e8c9f60f5f9304257569ae2d2c04b515b188e1bccab6007`
- review_ref: `83b4abfa-7633-4294-86a9-4a60a5b3eb71`

Initial specification_check_state: pass, coverage_status reviewed, no issues.
Approval checkpoint absent; the tool did not assign approval. Its mechanical
check does not independently prove semantic correctness or respondent identity.
The Approved Markdown and MCP-confirmed scope are frozen fixture inputs.
All four requirement definitions and both current decisions were read completely:
behavior `b3a22eec-4869-4b3f-93eb-0e9c3ff6f678@1` maps B1-001–004;
`scope.manifest@2` records the scope confirmation. Its nested proposal's
confirmed:false does not override the current confirmed manifest.

## Repository evidence and prerequisites

Reverify these locations before execution:

- `cli.mjs:2` reads only the command; `cli.mjs:3` owns exact help output,
  and `cli.mjs:4` reports UNKNOWN_COMMAND with exit 2.
- `test.mjs:4` checks the current help status and exact stdout.
- `test-process.mjs:6` exports runCli(args, { env }); lines 15–21 launch the
  real Node CLI using temporary stream file descriptors and return actual
  status, signal, stdout and stderr. Lines 22–25 clean up the capture files.
- `package.json:3` selects ES modules; `package.json:5` owns the installed
  single-file test command, node --test --test-isolation=none test.mjs.
- Planning observed Node v24.20.0 and a readable Git worktree with staged
  fixture files. Existing staged work belongs to the fixture; do not reset,
  restage, initialize Git, or require a clean tree. Inspect staged, unstaged
  and untracked paths before each packet.

Local Node and npm are existing runners; installation is forbidden. The user
authorizes planning only now. Each packet needs its own later explicit execution
instruction. All shell commands use rtk proxy and run from
`$TRIAL_ROOT/focused/q5-legacy/app`.

## Exactly two packets

| Packet | Outcome | Dependency | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [01](01_validation_and_validate.md) | Shared complete-input validator and validate CLI | Explicit execution authorization | B1-001, B1-002, B1-003 empty validate case, B1-004 |
| [02](02_summarize.md) | summarize consumes that validator | 01 complete with recorded passing evidence, plus explicit execution authorization | B1-002, B1-003, B1-004; B1-001 regression |

01 is independently verifiable without implementing summarize. 02 is independently
verifiable against the completed shared boundary; it must not duplicate validation.
Optional review and commits are not dependencies. The linked checklist in
[todo.md](todo.md) is the sole completion ledger.

## Proposed ownership and dependency direction

These are implementation-local choices, not changes to the frozen requirements.

| Unit / symbol | Purpose, inputs and outputs | Lifecycle, errors and invariants | Requirement / verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `records.mjs:parseRecords(bytes)` (new) | Pure boundary: complete file bytes to ordered array of {id, amount}, numeric amounts | Per-call decoder, array and Set; no global state or I/O. Fatal UTF-8 decoding; preserve any BOM for grammar rejection. Validate all rows before returning; reject malformed grammar, duplicate exact IDs and unsafe amounts with one internal invalid-input error. No prefix escapes on failure. | B1-001–003; table-driven parser checks plus CLI integration |
| `cli.mjs` data-command dispatch | Read the path completely with Node built-ins, call parseRecords, then serialize and write once | One invocation owns bytes/result. No output before complete validation; data input failure exits 2, stdout empty, stderr INVALID_INPUT followed by LF. Close file resources through built-in whole-file read. Keep help and unknown-command branches compatible. | B1-001–004; real runCli checks |
| `cli.mjs` validate result branch | Validated ordered records to JSON array | No second parser, no mutation of record values; success exit 0, empty stderr | B1-001–003; valid, empty and late-invalid integration cases |
| `cli.mjs` summarize result branch (02 only) | Same validated records to JSON {count,total} | Compute only after validation; count array length, total sum of amounts, zero identities for empty input; invocation-local accumulation | B1-002–004; expected aggregates and invalid corpus parity |
| `test.mjs` tests/fixture utilities | Temporary byte fixtures to assertions through runCli | Each fixture cleaned in finally; keep real subprocess and exact status/signal/stream assertions; preserve existing help check | B1-001–004; focused and full installed runner |
| `test-process.mjs:runCli` (preserved) | Real process capture for both packets | Existing fd capture/cleanup and env support unchanged; no imports or mocks substituting for CLI assertions | B1-004; preserve bytes and use throughout |

Dependency direction is CLI → shared parser → Node built-ins. Tests depend on the
CLI through runCli, and may additionally test the pure parser. The parser never
imports the CLI. Keep summary formatting local to the summarize branch rather
than introducing a service/class layer.

JSON formatting choice: compact output followed by LF for successes; assert exact
serialization for ordinary examples. Amount acceptance is governed by decimal
syntax and safe integer value, so leading zeroes are accepted and become numeric
values. IDs remain case-sensitive strings in input order, including __proto__.
Do not trim input, normalize CRLF, coerce signs/exponents or skip blank rows.
Empty bytes mean zero records; LF terminates a row rather than creating an empty
record, and blank rows (including a lone LF) are invalid.

No extra safe-integer restriction applies to the total. Use exact internal
integer accumulation (BigInt from validated numeric amounts) and serialize total
as an unquoted JSON decimal number, retaining the required JSON object shape.
This avoids imposing a new rejection on valid rows whose aggregate exceeds the
safe-integer limit. Do not expose BigInt in the records contract.

## Coverage and execution environments

| Requirement | Owning check |
| --- | --- |
| B1-001 | 01 exact help, ordered validate JSON, valid complete file; 02 regression |
| B1-002 | 01 full syntax/UTF-8/duplicate/range corpus and no partial stdout; 02 same corpus through summarize |
| B1-003 | 01 empty validate; 02 empty and multirow count/total |
| B1-004 | Both use one parser, built-ins only, unchanged harness/test command and unrelated bytes; 01 stops before 02 |

Planned checks run on the supplied local Node v24.20.0 fixture using the installed
npm test script. No cross-platform support matrix or additional minimum Node
version is specified; do not claim checks on other platforms. Missing runners or
an unreadable Git worktree block execution rather than permitting installation.

## Risks, operation and documentation

Whole-file validation deliberately buffers the input/result to satisfy atomic
output. No approved file-size limit or streaming/performance target exists; add
none. Fatal decoding and complete lexical checks avoid replacement-character,
whitespace and numeric-coercion acceptance. Error output contains only the fixed
token, never input contents. Read failures and a missing file operand should use
the same bounded data-input error path; no new command options are introduced.

No persistent data, migration, network, background process, retries, concurrency
coordination, logging subsystem or UI exists in this scope. Those concerns and
accessibility/design are not applicable. Local rollout is one packet at a time
after its tests pass. Recovery is a fresh invocation after correcting the file.
For implementation rollback, restore only the affected packet's code/tests from
its inspected pre-execution diff; never use broad Git reset or overwrite staged
fixture work. No external or irreversible step is included or authorized.

Durable developer documentation is not warranted: this is a localized CLI and
parser with one process, no operator configuration, and no new domain vocabulary.
The frozen spec owns the non-obvious grammar; fewer than two documentation
threshold signals apply. Therefore there is no third documentation packet.

## Handoff boundary

Before and after each future packet, reopen MCP context and check the pinned
aggregate source_version. Read only that packet's exact requirement sections

do not revise scope here. Before final planning handoff repeat the state check.

No tests or implementation packets are executed during planning. Planned RED,
GREEN and PROVE evidence belongs to future execution. Check [handoff.md](handoff.md)

# Packet Recovery

Read only when a packet's inputs conflict, verification fails, or incomplete
work is resumed. Diagnose before changing either implementation or acceptance.

## Identify The Cause

- **Implementation defect:** the check matches the current approved behavior
  and fails at the intended assertion. Correct implementation within the packet,
  rerun the focused check, and retain unrelated passing behavior.
- **Incorrect check:** current requirements or reproducible evidence contradict
  the check itself. Record the exact contradiction and why the corrected check
  still discriminates good from bad behavior. Correct the check, observe RED or
  PROVE as required, then verify implementation. A failing result alone is not
  evidence that a check is wrong. Ask before choosing between conflicting
  product interpretations; never weaken a correct check to obtain green.
- **Stale or incomplete input:** compare current requirement IDs and contract
  sections with the packet, manifest, and repository evidence. A moved symbol
  with unchanged behavior may be refreshed locally and recorded. Changed
  behavior, scope, dependencies, architecture, or acceptance requires the
  owning specification/planning workflow and separate authorization. Stop the
  affected work without rewriting its contract or generating a replacement plan.
- **Environment or harness failure:** record the command, working directory,
  actual exit/result, and missing prerequisite. A dependency/import/collection
  failure is not a behavioral RED; repair only authorized local prerequisites.
  Never install globally, bypass controls, skip a required check, or report
  an unavailable check as passed. Request new authority directly if needed.
  A replacement runner must preserve the observation layer, assertions,
  platform/dependency contract and required checks. Importing CLI code or
  assigning an exit-code property does not prove a real process exit; a mock
  does not replace required HTTP or browser evidence. If equivalence is not
  established, keep the check unavailable and ask about any material change.

For a missing material technical choice, checkpoint it and return the affected
task to separately invoked planning and its `references/technical-agreement.md`.
Implementation must not redesign or manufacture agreement in the handoff. Scope,
behavior or acceptance changes belong to specification. Continue only independent,
already authorized work that does not depend on the unresolved choice.

For unreadable or abbreviated tool output, use its published exact retrieval or
continuation mechanism. Do not count a summary as the required source read. If
exact content remains unavailable, record that input as unavailable and stop
dependent work. Do not cycle through encodings, character dumps or alternative
shell representations to defeat transport compression. Continue only unaffected
authorized work; output delivery failure does not authorize host reconfiguration.

## Preservation Conflicts

Compare the recorded baseline with actual packet writes, expected native
workflow transitions and independent external changes. Never require the entire
checkout to differ only in checklist/handoff files. Verify native binding
transitions through their owning scenario; do not hand-edit them or exempt the
whole workflow directory. Preserve external edits, inspect their overlap and
recheck affected inputs. An overlapping planned write, unknown content delta or
changed protected data is a blocker; do not silently accept the new baseline.
Git identity/history and file bytes remain protected. A directory timestamp
change alone is not evidence that their contents changed.

Correct a disproved check before rerunning it, record why the replacement still
detects loss, and retain the initial failure and recovery evidence. Do not relax
a valid check or automatically undo another writer's work.

## Resume And Handoff

Before bulk code reads or production edits, call `planning_packet_check` with
the packet's exact `agreement_ref` and `expected_proposal_digest`. Recheck after
implementation alongside the pinned specification check. A missing, stale or
blocked result stops affected work. Compare the scoped diff with the agreed
significant units, contracts, interactions and approach; behavioral tests alone
do not justify an architecture substitution. Record this comparison in handoff.
A private helper within the agreed boundary is flexible. A changed shared
signature, ownership, pattern or binding name returns to planning for a revised
proposal and explicit answer; product changes return to specification. A moved
existing symbol with unchanged meaning may be refreshed as evidence and recorded.

For legacy packets without qualifying agreement, preserve existing work and
return only the affected task to planning. Reuse adequate exact evidence where
possible, but require a managed ready binding before execution. Do not fabricate
references, bulk-migrate plans or rewrite completed tasks. Missing capability is
a concrete prerequisite, never permission to bypass the gate.

Recheck the packet's pinned completeness version through
`specification_check_state` before edits and before marking completion, following
`shared/references/yaml-contracts.md`. Review metadata alone does not invalidate
the specification; changed requirements, scope or source decisions do. Stale or
incomplete new-review inputs return to the specification owner. Do not silently
refresh a packet's version to conceal changed behavior. Legacy inputs remain
explicitly unverified, not automatically migrated.

Reconcile the current packet, checklist, handoff, scoped diff, and actual
verification evidence. Preserve user edits and unrelated work. Do not restart a
completed slice, assume a stale pass still applies, or trust an unchecked claim
from the previous agent. Reuse checks only while their inputs remain unchanged.
If work exists before its check, apply the shared PROVE rule.

Keep one compact current handoff with links to reusable private evidence, not
repeated inventories, transcripts or workflow instructions. Preserve executable
commands and material results. Replace the handoff's current state with: packet ID; complete/incomplete state;
changed paths; commands and working directories; expected versus actual results;
RED/GREEN/PROVE evidence; unresolved decisions and blocked prerequisites; and
the next eligible packet. A missing result remains unknown. Mark completion only
after every required check passes. Do not introduce an independent-review gate.

After completing or handing off the current packet, stop. User-requested fixes
to a completed packet are rework of that packet, not authority to start the next.
Neither an uncommitted previous packet nor absent optional review prevents a
new explicitly authorized packet whose actual dependencies are satisfied.

## Workflow YAML Access

Follow `shared/references/yaml-contracts.md`. Use `specification_open`,
`scope_get`, `decision_find` and `decision_get` for bounded current inputs.
Do not hand-edit workflow YAML while implementing a packet. A required scope or
design change goes back to its separately authorized owning workflow. Technical
questions and answers belong to planning's `planning_*` scenarios, not the
behavioral journal. Missing MCP blocks affected work, not permission to use a
shell reader or synthesize an answer.
